title: Algebraicity and prime-height drop for a nonzero monogenic kernel
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $S$ be a commutative domain, and let $f:R[T]\twoheadrightarrow S$ be a surjective $R$-algebra homomorphism from the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Assume the structure map $R\to S$ is injective and $\mathfrak n=\ker(f)$ is nonzero. A domain is a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors. Then the induced extension $\operatorname{Frac}(S)/\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ has finite vector-space dimension, and $\operatorname{trdeg}_R S=0$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$, put $Q=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$. Define residue fields by $\kappa(\mathfrak a)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak a)$ for a prime $\mathfrak a$ of a ring $A$, and heights as suprema of lengths of strict prime chains ending at the prime. The quotient-induced field isomorphism $\kappa(Q)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is an isomorphism over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and
$$\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)+1\leq\operatorname{ht}(Q).$$

source.place: Tag 02IJ (algebra-lemma-dimension-formula), proof, Case II: nonzero prime kernel, generic algebraicity, quotient residue fields, and height drop (before using Case I).

proof.text: Put $A=R[T]$, $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, $L=\operatorname{Frac}(S)$, and $x=f(T)\in S\subset L$. The injection $R\to S$ embeds $K$ in $L$ by $r/t\mapsto f(r)/f(t)$. Choose $0\ne P\in\mathfrak n$. Its coefficientwise image $P_K\in K[T]$ is nonzero, since $R\to K$ is injective. Because $f$ is an $R$-algebra map, $P_K(x)=f(P)=0$ in $L$. Thus $x$ is algebraic over $K$ [def-weil-algebraic-element].

source.place: Tag 02IJ (algebra-lemma-dimension-formula), Case II: the implicit generic polynomial relation

proof.text: Surjectivity gives $S=R[x]$: each $s\in S$ is $f(g)=g(x)$ for some $g\in R[T]$. Consequently $S\subseteq K(x)\subseteq L$, and every $a/b\in L$ with $a,b\in S$, $b\ne0$, belongs to the field $K(x)$. Hence $L=K(x)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] to the single algebraic element $x$ of $L$ over the field $K$. It gives that $L/K$ is a finite-dimensional vector space.

source.place: Tag 02IJ (algebra-lemma-dimension-formula), Case II, generic algebraicity; Fields Tag 09GH (fields-lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated), applied to one generator

proof.text: The finite $K$-algebra $L$ is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. For any $y\in S$, take its monic annihilating polynomial $H\in K[U]$. Write each coefficient as $a_i/b_i$ with $a_i,b_i\in R$ and $b_i\ne0$, and set $d=\prod_i b_i\ne0$. Then $dH$ has coefficients in $R$, has nonzero leading coefficient $d$, and vanishes at $y$ in $L$, hence in $S$. Every $y\in S$ therefore satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $R$. Any nonempty subset of $S$ contains such a $y$; its one-variable relation is a nonzero relation on that subset, so it is not algebraically independent. The empty subset is independent since $R\to S$ is injective. By [def-kun-transcendence-degree] the supremum of the cardinalities of independent subsets is $0$: $\operatorname{trdeg}_R S=0$.

source.place: Tag 02IJ (algebra-lemma-dimension-formula), Case II, trdeg_R(S)=0; Tag 00GK (algebra-lemma-finite-is-integral), after passage to fraction fields

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak q$, $Q=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and $\mathfrak p$ as in the statement. The map $e:A/Q\to S/\mathfrak q$, $a+Q\mapsto f(a)+\mathfrak q$, is well defined and injective by the definition of $Q$, and is surjective because $f$ is. For $r\in R$, its class maps to zero in either quotient exactly when $f(r)\in\mathfrak q$, equivalently $r\in\mathfrak p$. Thus $R/\mathfrak p$ embeds in both quotients, and $e$ commutes with these embeddings. On fractions it gives $\widetilde e:(a+Q)/(b+Q)\mapsto(f(a)+\mathfrak q)/(f(b)+\mathfrak q)$; a nonzero denominator stays nonzero by injectivity. Cross multiplication proves well-definedness, and applying $e^{-1}$ to numerator and denominator gives its inverse. This is $\kappa(Q)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. On each fraction of elements of $R/\mathfrak p$ the formula is the identity, proving compatibility with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Tag 02IJ (algebra-lemma-dimension-formula), Case II: the corresponding quotient prime has the same residue extension

proof.text: The ring $A=R[T]$ is a domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain], with one variable, so $(0)$ is prime. Take any strict chain $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_m=\mathfrak q$ in $S$. Its inverse images $Q_i=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)$ are prime: a product in $Q_i$ maps into the prime $\mathfrak q_i$, and $1\notin Q_i$. They remain strict: lift an element of $\mathfrak q_{i+1}\setminus\mathfrak q_i$ using surjectivity. Every $Q_i$ contains $\mathfrak n\ne0$, so $(0)\subsetneq Q_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Q_m=Q$ has length $m+1$. If the lengths in $S$ are unbounded, so are these lifted lengths; otherwise the set of lengths is nonempty (it contains the length-zero chain consisting of $\mathfrak q$) and its integer supremum is attained. In either case taking suprema gives $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)+1\le\operatorname{ht}(Q)$.
